title: About Grant Huston | Huston Logic
description: Grant Huston builds websites and AI-run systems for small businesses, checked the way a big software team would. One person, from the first call to the handoff.

content.title: Hi, I'm Grant. I like messy problems.
content.intro: Specifically, the kind that live between your website, your inbox and your spreadsheet.

content.heading: The short version
content.body: I'm the founder of Huston Logic and, for now, the whole team. I build websites and AI-run systems for small businesses, and I check them the way a big software team would.

content.heading: Why I do this
content.body: Big companies have teams to bring AI into how they work. A small business has the owner, usually after hours. I started Huston Logic to bring small businesses into the AI age, one useful system at a time, with no fluff and no upselling.

paragraphs.text: I started in 2020 as an intern at a startup, connecting their website, booking calendar and CRM so nobody had to retype a sign-up. After that I joined a global consulting firm and ran the app that 50-plus consultants used on large bankruptcy cases. Reports from it went to court. Every change was tested before release, and releases went out every other Friday evening. (I got very good at Friday evenings.)

In 2024 I started building systems for small businesses. My first big project was a group therapy practice that had outgrown doing everything by hand. I built the team a staff app, payroll submissions, an inquiry pipeline and dashboards, and the practice went on to grow from 5 to 10 people. Next came a personal training studio whose owner wanted real numbers on his coaches and clients, without giving up the scheduling app his team already used.

In 2026 I joined a Zoho consulting partner as a developer and moved into a consulting role within a few months. There, I led delivery for 21 client accounts: a Medicaid disability services provider, an interior design firm, a newly formed distributor, a wholesaler, a municipal government and more, often directing a team of developers. I learned a lot about what makes projects succeed, and about what happens when a business gets a system that's bigger than its problem.
So I started Huston Logic to do the work I like most: close to the owner, focused on the real problem, and sized to the business.

Since then I've worked with tech startups, therapy practices, fitness studios and structural engineering firms. Most were getting by on a template and a workaround, because custom software was priced for companies with an IT department.
That's what changed. AI does the slow parts of a build now, and I kept the habit from the big firm: nothing ships untested.

content.heading: Why websites too
content.body: A website is where most of my clients' inquiries start, and the contact form is the first system a business has. So I build those too, starting with this site. AI does the slow parts of the build, so the price doesn't have to cover them. I design every page and check it myself before you see it. I've spent my career where software meets business, as an application developer, business analyst and software consultant. Checking what AI builds is the same work, done faster.

content.heading: What working with me is like
content.intro: Every project runs the same three steps: **{stepsList}.** In practice:
items: **I listen first.** Before I suggest anything, I make sure I understand how your business actually works.
**I start with what you have.** New software isn't always the answer. Often the fix is a setting, a process or a connection between tools you already pay for.
**You see the price before I build.** The plan says what's included, what isn't, and what it costs.
**I try to break it before you see it.** Then I fix what broke.
**It's yours to take.** Your team is trained, the handoff is written down, and I hand everything over whenever you ask.
**I tell you the truth.** If you don't need a build, I'll say so.

content.heading: What I bring
items: Website design and build, on fast hosting that I run for you
Zoho, deeply: CRM, Creator, Analytics, Books, Desk, Flow, Forms and the rest of the suite
Integrations and automations across many other tools
Dashboards and reporting people actually use
Requirements, process mapping, testing and training
Experience with healthcare and other sensitive data, where the agreements and access controls come first

Years of consulting experience across small businesses and large enterprises, and the boring certifications to go with it. I've seen how all kinds of small businesses, from therapists and interior design firms to wealth management and structural engineering, use technology to take the next step: automating the busywork so their people can get on with the real work.

content.heading: Off the clock
content.body: I was born and raised in Southern California, and I'm recently married (September 2026). My wife and I like going on adventures, and my cat likes to supervise from a distance. I also play blues guitar and write songs, which turns out to be decent training for this work: listen first, keep time, and make the parts fit together. The rest of the time it's horror movies, video games, concerts, comedy shows and hunting down the best restaurants in town. I like building for people I'd want to work with anyway.
